exposure: Premature rupture of membranes (PROM) at term
outcome: Maternal complications (chorioamnionitis, puerperal fever, postpartum hemorrhage)
Neonatal complications (birth asphyxia, meconium aspiration syndrome, NICU admissions)
cohort: The study included 200 pregnant women diagnosed with PROM after 37 completed weeks of gestation.
finding: PROM at term is associated with significant maternal and neonatal morbidity, with observed incidences of chorioamnionitis (6%), puerperal fever (15%), postpartum hemorrhage (5%), birth asphyxia (10.5%), meconium aspiration syndrome (7%), and NICU admissions (12.5%).
followup_time: The last observations were taken at the end of the hospital stay, averaging 4.4 days for mothers and 4.48 days for neonates.
